newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.00-dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.00-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Thursday were $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower amid light demand from packers stuffed with live hog inventories, livestock dealers said.
Ample hog movement following the Memorial Day holiday weekend provided more than enough hogs needed for this short slaughter week, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower in light activity at $54.50 to $55.50 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants, dealers and packer buyers there said.
Illinois hogs sold $1.00 lower at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and up to $56.00 at plants.
Indiana hogs sold $1.00 lower at $54.50 to $55.50 in the country and $56.00 to $56.50 at plants. Ohio hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $52.00 to $53.00 in the country and $55.00 to $56.50 at plants.
Losses were furthered by steep declines in pork cutout values on Wednesday, although the lower prices succeeded in moving some pork, sources noted.
Pork cut-out prices Wednesday were quoted down $0.96 to $1.01 per cwt, USDA reported.
A total of 130.50 loads of pork cuts and 73.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold, USDA statistics showed.
